name: Wella

lead: Wella is a hair-care and cosmetics company founded in Germany in 1880 and now headquartered in Geneva. It supplies salons with hair colour, styling and treatment products, and its portfolio includes brands such as ghd, OPI, Nioxin, Sebastian Professional and Clairol.

For appearance, Wella products are tools for changing hair colour, covering greys, adding tone or shine, and styling. Results come from permanent or demi-permanent colour lines such as Koleston, applied in salons or at home.

paras: Colour is usually applied by a stylist, who chooses the shade and developer and sets the processing time; home-use lines also exist. Toners and conditioning treatments are used between colouring appointments, and colour fades over weeks, so many people repeat it.
Hair dye can cause scalp irritation or allergic reactions in some people, and product instructions advise patch testing before use. Bleaching and repeated colouring can dry or weaken hair.

angle.text: Wella's professional colour and styling lines change hair colour and finish, covering greys or adding tone. The effect lasts until the colour fades or grows out.

lead: Wella is a hair-care and cosmetics company that began in 1880 when hairdresser Franz Stroher started making tulle for wigs in Rothenkirchen, Saxony, later expanding into permanent wave equipment and hair care; the Wella trademark was registered in 1924 [1]. It is now based in Geneva and operates in more than 150 countries [1].

For looks, the brand is relevant through hair colour and styling. Its Koleston range was introduced in 1950 and Koleston Perfect in 1995, and in 2014 the company patented the ME+ molecule as an alternative to the dye ingredients PPD and PTD [1].
The company has changed hands several times: Procter and Gamble acquired a majority stake in 2003, Coty bought it in 2015, and in 2020 it became independent, majority-owned by KKR [1].
infobox: Wella Professionals, ghd, OPI, Nioxin, Sebastian Professional, Clairol, Briogeo

paras: Franz Stroher began in 1880 making tulle for wigs; the family rebuilt the business in West Germany in 1945-46 as Ondal GmbH, renamed Wella AG in Darmstadt by 1950 [1]. Koleston launched in 1950, Wella Balsam in 1972, Koleston Perfect in 1995 and TrendVision in 2002 [1].

Procter and Gamble bought a majority stake in 2003 for about US$5.7 billion. In 2015 Coty acquired Wella in a deal valued around US$12.5 billion for P&G's specialty beauty business. In 2020 Wella became independent under majority ownership by KKR, and in 2022 it acquired the haircare brand Briogeo [1].
Brands under the company include Wella Professionals, ghd, OPI, Nioxin, Sebastian Professional, Clairol and Briogeo [1].
